description_en: Mahendra Dhārā (Fountain), which has ancient components dating from the 13th to the 18th century, is located in the locality of Kaḍāyata Village, situated one kilometre east of Vināyaka. The Fountain is made of a 2 x 4 metres stone paved basin. In the basin's northwest corner, a small stone water reservoir is constructed. Steps are built on the SE and NW sides. Water enters the fountain through one main stone slab carved with a half-pipe on the fountain’s northwest wall.  To the right of the latter, another similar small slab is placed in the masonry.When the site was documented in April 2022 CE, there was no water coming out of the Fountain. A round shaped carved stone element protrudes from the wall to the left. Based on its eroded state, this element appears to be of some age, possibly dating from the 13th and 18th centuries. At first glance, it appears to be amakarawater spout, but closer inspection reveals that there is no hole for water to pass through. The original purpose of this element is unknown, but itsmakara-like shape is likely what drew the fountain's builders to incorporate it into the masonry.Above the main water spout is a stone slab with an inscription recording the name of the Fountain, Mahendra Dhārā, and the date of its construction VS 2020 (1964 CE).
monument_assessment: Good (very few light surface damages, renovated or repaired)

historical_events.event_description: The stone slab inscription above the spout records that the Fountain was built during the reign of King Mahendra (who reigned from 1955 CE to his death in 1972 CE) and named ‘Fivefold Venerable Mahendra Dhārā”.The inscription reads:Śrī(written on top margin)Line1:śrī 5 mahendra dhārāḥ(!)Line2:a. ma. bhai. bināyakaLine3:grāma pañcāyataLine4:pra. paṃ. rana bahādura kaḍāyataLine5:kṣetrīLine6:samba(!)ta 2020 sāla bhādraLine7:2 gate roja 1 māḥ(!) ||
